title: Crispy Roasted Potatoes
description: Yukon Gold potato chunks roasted on a preheated pan in a hot oven until deep golden and crisp outside, with garlic and rosemary.
scaleNote: One large rimmed sheet pan holds 2 pounds of potatoes with room between the pieces. For more, heat a second pan and swap the pans' positions when you flip the potatoes.

image.alt: Illustration of golden roasted potato chunks with rosemary on a sheet pan

ingredients.prep: scrubbed and cut into {len 1 1/2 in} chunks

steps.text: Put a large rimmed sheet pan on the middle rack and heat the oven to {temp 450F oven}. Heating the pan with the oven means the potatoes start browning the moment they touch it.

Pat the potato chunks very dry with a clean towel; water left on the surface turns to steam and keeps the outsides soft. Toss them in a large bowl with the oil, salt and pepper until every piece is coated.

Using oven mitts, take out the hot pan and tip the potatoes onto it; they will sizzle. Spread them in a single layer, cut sides down, with a little space between pieces. Crowded potatoes steam instead of crisping.
Roast without stirring until the undersides are deep golden and release easily from the pan, {time 20-25 min}.

Flip the potatoes with a thin metal spatula and sprinkle with the garlic powder and rosemary. Roast until crisp all over and tender when pierced with a knife, {time 15-20 min}. Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed.

notes: If the potatoes stick when you try to flip them, give them {time 3-5 min notimer} more. They let go once a crust has formed.
Russet potatoes work too. They come out fluffier inside but break up more easily when you flip them.
Leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 4 days. Reheat them on a sheet pan in a {temp 425F oven} oven for {time 10 min notimer} to bring back the crunch; the microwave makes them soft.
